h: Herders, Hills and a Little Bit of Lapland
p: The reindeer here have a story worth telling the kids on the drive up. They were brought over from Sweden in 1952 by a Sami herder called Mikel Utsi and his wife, Dr Ethel Lindgren, who reckoned the Cairngorms looked like perfect reindeer country. They were right, and the herd has roamed these mountains ever since, making them Britain's only free-ranging reindeer. That bit of history makes the whole day feel even more special.

A few practical thoughts. The walk to the herd is on a hill path, so this isn't one for prams; little ones who can't manage it are better off in a back carrier. The reindeer are gentle, but they've got antlers and opinions, so listen carefully to the herders' instructions about feeding and keep fingers flat. Mountain weather can change quickly even in summer, so pack a hat and gloves alongside the sun cream, and a flask of something hot for afterwards goes down a treat.

In and around Aviemore there's loads more for families. The Strathspey Railway runs heritage steam trains from Aviemore through Boat of Garten to Broomhill, a lovely gentle way to see the strath from a carriage window. Rothiemurchus estate has forest trails and outdoor activities, and the Highland Wildlife Park at Kincraig, a short drive south, adds wildcats, snow monkeys and polar bears to your wildlife tally. If the clouds lift, the CairnGorm Mountain area gives you big views over the whole range. Few places in Britain pack so much wild stuff into one valley.
